transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brought me in is that... some evenings after work, especially when I've been really strict all day, I just end up eating way more than I meant to. Like, I'll eat dinner, and then... then I'll have cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are around, and sweets, all within just a couple of hours. It's just... it's been bothering me, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control what you're eating during those episodes?

Yeah, I do. It's like... once I get started on those nights, I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just keep eating. I don't really feel back in charge of things until I'm uncomfortably full.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating are over?

Yes, I do. Um... I feel really guilty about it. It's just frustrating because... well, I know better, you know? I should be able to control myself. So, yeah, I definitely feel pretty ashamed once it's all over and I realize how much I actually just ate.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during those episodes?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm rushing or eating super fast. It's more just... a steady pace of eating that goes on for a while. I'm just constantly eating over those couple of hours, rather than wolfing it all down in a few minutes.
How often do these episodes of eating more than you meant to happen?

For the past few months, I'd say it happens most weeks. It's usually about one or two nights a week where I end up eating far more than I planned to. And then... well, the next day I always try to make up for it. I'll usually skip meals, or I'll spend a lot more time exercising just to try and fix what I did the night before.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these eating episodes?
No, I don't do that. I've never made myself throw up. Um... I just try to handle it by skipping meals the next day or doing extra exercise, like I mentioned. But no, no vomiting.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
No, not really. My weight has stayed pretty steady, honestly. I mean, maybe it fluctuates a pound or two up or down depending on the week, but I haven't noticed any significant changes.
Do you do anything else to try and make up for the extra food you ate during those episodes?

No, not really. Um, just what I mentioned before. I just stick to skipping meals or doing that extra workout. I don't take anything or do anything else to try and fix it... just the fasting and the exercise.
Do you think the reason you skip meals or exercise more after these episodes is to try not to gain weight from all the extra food you ate?

Yeah, exactly. That's why I do it. The next day after one of those nights, I'll just tell myself I'm making up for it so I don't gain weight. I'll skip breakfast and lunch, or I'll go out for an extra-long hike... or I'll push myself a lot harder at softball conditioning, even when I'm already really tired. I just feel like I have to balance it out.
Do you think you'd still try to make up for those extra calories through exercise or skipping meals if you didn't think it would help you avoid gaining weight?

I don't know, honestly. I've never really thought about it like that. I guess... if I knew it wouldn't make a difference with my weight, I probably wouldn't push myself so hard. The whole point of skipping the meals or doing the extra workouts is just to make sure I don't gain anything from what I ate.
Do you think you would still feel the need to eat in this way if you didn't worry about gaining weight?

I don't think so. I mean, the whole reason I eat like that—the binging, I guess—it's usually because I've been restricting myself so much trying to keep my weight down. If I didn't care about my weight, I probably wouldn't restrict in the first place, and then I wouldn't end up losing control like that. So, no, I don't think I would.
Do you think there are any other factors, besides trying to control your weight, that contribute to your episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Um... no, not really. I can't think of anything else. I mean, it really just comes down to the fact that I get so hungry from trying not to eat all day. I haven't really noticed any other reason for it besides just trying to keep my weight down.
Do you have a persistent fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even when you're at a healthy weight?

I don't know if I'd call it a fear, exactly. I mean... I definitely don't want to gain weight, but I'm not terrified of it or anything. I just prefer to keep my weight where it is, so I try to manage it. But I wouldn't say I'm constantly scared of becoming fat.
Do you think your efforts to control your weight are excessive?

Um... no, I wouldn't say they're excessive. I mean, I just try to watch what I eat and keep things in check. It feels pretty normal to me, just standard dieting, really. I know I restrict a bit too much sometimes, which causes the other issue, but the actual effort to control my weight... no, I don't think I'm going to extremes or anything.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't have your menstrual period?

Um, no, not really. My periods have always been pretty regular. I mean, obviously at my age things are starting to change a bit now, but I never had a time where they just stopped completely when I was younger or anything like that.
Do you think there's something specifically wrong with your relationship with food or eating, beyond just trying to control your weight?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, food is just food to me. I know I have those times where I eat too much and then feel like I need to fix it, but I don't think there's some deep, complicated issue with how I view eating. It really just comes down to trying to keep my weight in check and sometimes messing up. So, no, I don't think there's anything else wrong beyond that.
Do you think your eating habits and the way you try to control your weight are causing you significant distress or problems in your daily life?

Um, not significant problems, no. I'm still keeping up with all my clients at work, and my mentoring role, plus all my responsibilities at home. Everything gets done. But... I guess I do get a little distracted by it sometimes. Like, if I have a public event or something coming up, I can feel less confident if I'm worrying about how my clothes are fitting. So it bothers me a bit then, but overall, I wouldn't say it's stopping me from living my life.
Do you think your eating habits are significantly interfering with your social or occupational functioning?

No, I wouldn't say they're significantly interfering. Like I was just saying, I'm still keeping up with everything. My clients are taken care of, I'm still doing my mentoring at work, and everything at home is getting done. It's just... well, like I mentioned, I can get distracted by it. If I have a public event or a big meeting, I might feel less confident if I'm worried about how my clothes are fitting. But it's not stopping me from doing my job or seeing people.
Do these episodes of eating more than you meant to, followed by restricting or exercising to make up for it, happen at least once a week for the past three months?

Yes, I'd say so. For the past few months, it's been happening most weeks. Usually, it's one or two nights a week where I just eat way more than I meant to. And then, you know, the next day I'll try to make up for it by skipping meals or pushing myself to exercise longer than usual. So, yeah, at least once a week.
Have these episodes of eating more than you meant to, followed by trying to make up for it, been happening for at least three months?

Yeah, I think we just covered that. Like I said, for the past few months it's been happening most weeks. It's usually one or two nights where I end up eating way more than I planned, and then the next day I try to fix it by skipping meals or exercising a lot more. So, yes, it's been going on for at least three months.
